A_target.statement:
Let $K$ be a [[Definition:Field (Abstract Algebra)|field]].
Then the [[Definition:Determinant of Matrix|determinant]] $\det: \map {\MM_K} n \to K$ is the [[Definition:Unique|unique]] [[Definition:Alternating Mapping|alternating]] [[Definition:Multilinear Mapping|multilinear]] function of the [[Definition:Column of Matrix|columns]] such that:
:$\map \det {\mathbf I_n} = 1$

B_source.statement:
Let $V$ be a [[Definition:Vector Space|vector space]] of [[Definition:Dimension of Vector Space|dimension]] $n$ over $K$.
Then the space of [[Definition:Alternating Mapping|alternating]] $n$-[[Definition:Multilinear Mapping|linear forms]] on $V$ has dimension $1$:
:$\map \dim {\bigwedge^n V^*} = 1$

validity_conditions: The space of alternating n-linear forms on an n-dimensional space is 1-dimensional, so fixing the value on one basis (det(I)=1) pins down a unique form.
Instantiating that unique normalized form on matrix columns yields exactly the determinant - a direct specialization, no new argument.
proof_plan: From the source result, the alternating $n$-linear forms on an $n$-dimensional space form a space of dimension $1$.
Take $V = K^n$, regarding an $n \times n$ matrix as the $n$-tuple of its [[Definition:Column of Matrix|columns]].

Any non-zero alternating form $\omega$ has $\map \omega {e_1, \ldots, e_n} \ne 0$.
Requiring the value $1$ on $\mathbf I_n$ selects a [[Definition:Unique|unique]] form.
